name: adapt_compounding_rate_python_dynamic
description: Dynamic eval, COMPOUNDING: two disruptions fire at the SAME prompt boundary (after_prompt 1), applied in declaration order so the second's write is what sticks - pricing.RATE changes twice before the agent's second turn
prompts: pricing.py exports RATE. Create quote.py with a function quote(amount) that returns amount * (1 + RATE), reading RATE live from pricing.py.
pricing.py's RATE may have changed one or more times since you last checked. Make sure quote() reflects the CURRENT value of RATE, however many times it has changed.

disruptions.description: RATE changed 0.05 -> 0.08 (first of two compounding changes)
RATE changed 0.08 -> 0.12 (second of two compounding changes, this is the one that sticks)

test_setup_files.test_quote.py:
import importlib.util
pricing_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('pricing_mod', 'pricing.py')
pricing_mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(pricing_spec)
pricing_spec.loader.exec_module(pricing_mod)
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('quote_mod', 'quote.py')
mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
want = 100 * (1 + pricing_mod.RATE)
got = mod.quote(100)
assert abs(got - want) < 1e-6, f'quote(100) = {got}, want {want} (the CURRENT RATE after both compounding changes)'
print('PASS')
